This page covers what is specific to the NOAA NMFS SEDNA cluster. Once you are
set up here, RiboPilot works as in the [Get started](RiboPilot.html)
walkthrough, with `executor = "NOAA_SEDNA"`.
[Running on a cluster](Clusters.html) explains how RiboPilot uses a cluster in
general.

You need a SEDNA account; see the
[account instructions](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1nn0T0OWEsQCBoCdaH6DSY69lQSbK3XnPlseyyQuU2Lc/edit?usp=sharing),
or contact Krista Nichols (<krista.nichols@noaa.gov>).

# First-time setup

RiboPilot needs Nextflow, Singularity, and R. On SEDNA, put all three in one
Mamba environment; installing RiboPilot with the cluster's R module runs into
problems.

Log in to the NOAA NMFS VPN, then to SEDNA. If you have never used Mamba on
SEDNA, run this once:

```bash
/opt/bioinformatics/mambaforge/bin/mamba init
```

Create the environment. This may take a while.

```bash
mamba create --name RiboPilot_deps 'bioconda::nextflow>=24.10,<25.11' \
  conda-forge::singularity conda-forge::zlib 'conda-forge::r-base>=4.4' -y
```

Then install RiboPilot into it:

```bash
mamba activate RiboPilot_deps
R
```

In that R session, follow step 5 of
[Install the tools](Installation.html#install-the-tools), then leave R with
`quit()`.

To upgrade later, activate `RiboPilot_deps` first, then follow
[Upgrading RiboPilot](Installation.html#upgrading-ribopilot).

# Open the app

The app needs little computing power, since the heavy work goes to the queue.
Start a small interactive session, note the name of the node it gives you, and
start R:

```bash
srun -c 2 --mem=16GB -p standard --pty /bin/bash
hostname
mamba activate RiboPilot_deps
R
```

In R, create a project (once), then open the app without a browser:

```r
RiboPilot::new_test_project(
  path = "/path/to/RiboPilot/test_project",
  executor = "NOAA_SEDNA"
)
RiboPilot::RiboPilot("/path/to/RiboPilot/test_project",
  host = "0.0.0.0", port = 8123, launch.browser = FALSE)
```

Use the same `executor = "NOAA_SEDNA"` with `RiboPilot::new_project()` for your
own data. Keep projects on shared project or scratch space, not in your home
folder. [Disk space, caches, and offline use](Caches-and-Offline.html) shows how
to move Singularity's caches and the reference folder there too.

On your own computer, open a tunnel to that node, using the name `hostname`
printed:

```bash
ssh -N -L 8123:<node>:8123 <user>@sedna.nwfsc2.noaa.gov
```

Enter your password; if it works, nothing more is printed. Then open
http://localhost:8123 in Chrome or Firefox. Leave both terminals open while you
use the app.

::: {.alert .alert-warning}
**The app has no login.** Other SEDNA users can reach its port. Pick an unusual
port number, and close the app when you are done.
:::

# Run the pipeline

Press **Update**. The run window shows a Slurm job script for the `standard`
partition. Press **Submit as job**, or **Save script** to submit it yourself
with `sbatch`. The job keeps going after you close the browser and the
interactive session. Watch it with `squeue`, then press the reload button above
the table to see new results.
[Submit a run as a job](Clusters.html#submit-a-run-as-a-job) has the details.

The job needs Nextflow and Singularity. A job submitted from the app inherits
the `RiboPilot_deps` environment. If you submit a saved script from a new
terminal, run `mamba activate RiboPilot_deps` there first.
